ARK: Survival Ascended is an incredibly fun and engaging game. The thrill of taming dinosaurs, building your base, and exploring the vast worlds keeps players coming back for more. The transition to Unreal Engine 5 has only made the game more immersive and exciting, offering a fresh experience that old and new players alike can enjoy. However, the recent decision to put Astraeos, a community-created map, behind a paywall has left a sour taste for many. Historically, maps like Ragnarok, Valguero, Crystal Isles, and Fjordur were made available for free, contributing significantly to ARK’s growth and success. The introduction of a paid community map now risks alienating the community and discouraging new players, especially when other games continue to offer free updates. This decision goes against the spirit of collaboration and accessibility that ARK has built over the years. Instead of charging for a map that was once freely available, Wildcard could focus on releasing fresh, original content that provides real value to the players. Additionally, locking community content behind paywalls creates division within the player base, making it feel less inclusive. It’s disheartening to see a game that has thrived on community involvement start to introduce barriers that could harm the very community that helped make it great. ARK is still an amazing game, but these choices risk undermining its legacy and the trust of its players.

The game is very poorly optimized. Is it fun? Yes, when it works. Is it worth buying? That depends entirely on how much you can tolerate constant crashes, bugs, and a lack of communication from the developers.

The gameplay itself can be genuinely enjoyable, but the experience is repeatedly ruined by frequent issues. The game receives updates almost daily, which would normally be a good thing, but in Wildcard’s case they rarely fix existing problems and often introduce new ones. It feels like prioritizing revenue over proper development.

If you read the discussions or look into the current state of the game, you’ll see that the general consensus is that it’s in a very rough condition, with no clear plans to improve. Despite all this, the core game is fun—but you have to be willing to deal with more technical problems than actual gameplay.

For now, I can’t recommend it.

tldr.text: Mixed (60%): players praise the graphics and the co-op with friends.
34% of reviews complain about bugs and crashes, the most common complaint.

details.text: Recent reviews complain about bugs and crashes far less often than before, though some still call it a "broken game".
Players in their first hours are far less positive, at 28%, than those who have played longer.

reason.text: Negative reviews focus on bugs, crashes and poor optimisation, and some tie each update to a full reinstall of the game.
Other reviews object to paying for new DLC and releases, which one reviewer says is designed to milk players.
